articleTitle: Path planning of mobile robot utilizing an enhanced version of the A*_TEB algorithm
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: To solve the problem of low quality and long path of traditional A* algorithm, A novel path planning algorithm combining improved A* algorithm with Time Elastic Band (TEB) algorithm is proposed. Firstly, enhancements are made to the traditional A* algorithm by OPENLIST updating, path de-redundancy and path smoothing. Subsequently, the kinematic modeling of the mobile robot is carried out and the TEB algorithm is used to optimize the path, which is in line with the kinematic characteristics of the mobile robot. Finally, the improved A*_TEB algorithm is improved to generate a fusion path planning algorithm and simulation and physical verification are carried out. The experimental results show that when the fusion algorithm is used for path planning, the generated global path is smooth and does not collide with obstacles and the local path meets the dynamic constraints of the robot. Compared with the traditional A* algorithm, the path is shortened by 14.6%, the planning time is shortened by 3.9% and the number of turns is reduced by 25%.

articleTitle: Lateral and longitudinal hierarchical control of port AGV path tracking based on MPC and SMC
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: To improve the accuracy and stability of AGV (Automated Guided Vehicle) path tracking in ports, and to address the issue of large lateral impact on tires during turns, a lateral and longitudinal hierarchical control strategy is proposed. The MPC (Model Predictive Control) lateral controller is constructed based on the AGV’s dynamics model. The SMC (Sliding Mode Control) longitudinal controller is built on a first-order inertial system, and the PI (Proportion Integration) controller is used to implement the drive or brake control of the AGV. Finally, under the joint Simulink and Trucksim simulation platform, the no-load motion performance of AGVs under typical working conditions is tested and verified. The simulation results show that the proposed control strategy can meet the parking accuracy and curve driving stability requirements of port AGVs, and the tire force during turning is small.

articleTitle: Effect of scanning strategy on the mechanical properties of honeycombs fabricated by selective laser melting of 316 L stainless steel
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Selective Laser Melting (SLM) is an advanced and widely adopted method in metal additive manufacturing. The scanning strategy serves as a crucial process parameter, significantly impacting the quality of the fabricated components, primarily due to the layer-by-layer bottom-up building nature of the process. This research investigates the influence of three different scanning strategies on the tensile mechanical characteristics of 316 L stainless steel produced via SLM. Additionally, it analyses the underlying mechanisms through which these scanning strategies exert their effects. Furthermore, different scanning strategies based on SLM are used to prepare the arc curved honeycomb structure, and the quasi-static compression response of the honeycomb is compared. The findings highlight that the strip scanning strategy with an interlayer rotation angle of 67°proves advantageous for enhancing both the tensile properties of SLM-produced 316 L stainless steel and the compressive strength of the honeycomb structures.

articleTitle: A scenario-based synchronization framework for construction logistics scheduling in urban areas
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: A method that boosts the effectiveness of construction logistics is logistics scheduling for on-site and off-site construction in a hybrid paradigm. Inspired by the telecommunications routing system, a two-stage scheduling model with LAN (local area network) and WAN (wide area network) logistics scheduling is proposed. The WAN logistics scheduling focuses on the coordination of cross-city logistics. And the LAN logistic scheduling focuses on logistics in urban areas. A four-step LAN logistics scheduling method is designed, containing: arrival schedule, schedule modification, LAN logistics schedule, and schedule confirmation. A case study is conducted with a BIM-GIS-based residential construction model to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed logistic scheduling problem.

articleTitle: Research on the configuration of AS/RS warehouse system based on AGV transportation
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Compared to traditional AS/RS warehousing systems that use conveyor belts or manual labor to transport goods in and out of storage, AS/RS warehousing systems that use AGVs for transport operations have advantages in high area utilization, work efficiency, and system flexibility. This article constructs an open queuing network model for AGV-AS/RS outbound operations, establishes performance analysis indicators for average service time of outbound orders, order queue length, and AGV utilization, and analyzes the impact of outbound temporary storage points and AGV configuration on the performance of AGV-AS/RS warehousing system under different order arrival rates. Through FlexSim simulation of the warehousing system, it was found that the accuracy of the established mathematical model for this warehousing system is greater than 85%, which verifies the effectiveness of the model. Finally, Comparative analysis shows that the storage system using AGV as a transportation tool has an average performance improvement of 30% compared to using forklifts.

articleTitle: Macroscopic traffic model with variable optimal density of traffic flow
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: The traditional traffic flow equations of road derive the optimal density only with the blockage density(kj), but not with the maximum road speed limit or free flow speed(vf), the calculation results vary greatly; some other models will be the optimal density(km) as input conditions, need to be given by empirical formulas or a priori parameters; With the improvement of vehicle performance and the promotion of road speed limits, there are some unavoidable difficulties in the traditional models to explain the traffic flow problem. The paper starts from the safety of following driving, and uses the calculus equivalence relationship between the microscopic following criterion and macroscopic traffic flow three-parameter model to construct a fundamental diagram traffic model for determining the optimal density by the free flow velocity; according to the different characteristics of the non-congested section and congested section of the traffic flow, three fitting expressions of free flow with different traffic velocity decaying according to density are proposed for high-speed limit and medium, low-speed limit roads. The results show that the proposed equations reveal that the traffic waves generated in congested areas are constant velocity backward traffic waves, which is supported by the empirical results of the relevant authoritative literature.

articleTitle: Hybrid optimization for scheduling budget-constrained energy-aware workflows in the cloud
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Cloud computing become a popular environment for deploying compute- and data-intensive scientific applications. However, scheduling workflows in cloud datacenters efficiently to meet all parties’ requirements is still a great challenge. This paper proposes a hybrid optimization approach, GBO+GA, which combines the Gradient-Based Optimizer (GBO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA) for scheduling workflows to minimize the makespan under budget and energy consumption constraints. Firstly, an evolution-aware update strategy switching mechanism is designed to use GBO and GA alternatively in the right time and thus to improve the search diversity. Second, a pattern learning-based auxiliary GBO is adopted to update individuals when the whole population gets stuck into local optima, i.e., replacing the best guiding solution in the original GBO with the defined pattern to make the population escape from local optima and explore more potential areas around. Third, to improve the average fitness of the whole population, some bottom ranked individuals are guided by the global best individual to move towards the optimal solution and speed up convergence. Extensive experiments are conducted on four well-known scientific workflows with different scales, and results demonstrate that GB+GA outperforms its peers, GA, GBO and PSO in the success rate, solution quality and convergence.

articleTitle: Hybrid mechanism-data-driven method for energy consumption estimation model of shore bridge
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Energy consumption acquisition of single equipment is of great significance to port energy consumption management. The existing methods for energy consumption acquisition of single equipment are complicated, cumbersome ， and not feasible. We propose a hybrid mechanism-data-driven energy consumption prediction method based on a support vector machine (SVM), which is selected by a whale optimization algorithm (WOA) on a hyperparameter. In this paper, the proposed algorithm is evaluated by using the measured energy consumption data of the shore bridge, and two comparison experiments are designed. The results indicate that the proposed WOA-SVM-based hybrid mechanism-data-driven energy consumption model can be used for shore bridge energy consumption prediction and has higher prediction accuracy compared with other prediction methods.

articleTitle: A hybrid algorithm for a flexible resource-constrained multi-project assembly scheduling
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Project scheduling is essential for enhancing project execution efficiency and success rates through effective time and resource management. This study investigates a manufacturing process involving multiple products, framing it as a multi-project assembly scheduling problem with flexible resources. The primary objective is to minimize both project completion time and average flow time by optimizing project sequences and resource allocation. To achieve this, we develop a comprehensive activity sequence by integrating individual project sequences using two heuristics. A mathematical model is formulated to address these objectives, and an iterative hybrid NSGA-II with Tabu search (HNSGATS) is introduced to enhance decision-making variables. In this algorithm, resources are assigned to available activities upon their completion, with the resource exhibiting the highest availability selected as a substitute to expedite the initiation of subsequent activities. Each iteration explores various neighbourhood structures for project sequences and substitute resources, aiming to identify improved solutions. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in achieving optimal results.

articleTitle: The ecological evolution of logistics industry clusters in two major cities along the Yellow River Basin
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: This paper examines the evolutionary process of logistics industry cluster development in the Yellow River Basin, using ecological population-related theory as a framework. By analyzing Lotka-Volterra competitive and symbiotic evolution patterns under the influence of stagnation, it is revealed that when competition between logistics industry clusters is moderate, their ecological evolution reaches a stable equilibrium. The spatial distribution of logistics industry clusters in the Yellow River Basin is characterized by distinct patterns, which are summarized along with the evolutionary process and development law. Based on these findings, an optimization scheme is proposed to promote the ecological and orderly evolution of logistics industry clusters in the Yellow River Basin. This study contributes to a deeper understanding of the dynamic of logistics industry cluster development and provides valuable insights for further research.

articleTitle: Study on the distribution of passenger ridership intensity and network efficiency at metro stations considering land factors
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Currently, research in rail transit passenger flow primarily focuses on prediction, with limited attention to the mechanisms of how land use affects passenger flow. Furthermore, studies on network efficiency in this context rarely consider both passenger-weighted and land-weighted factors. This paper integrates subway passenger Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) data and collects Point of Interest (POI) data for the areas around stations. It defines multi-level impact zones centered around stations and utilizes station clustering algorithms along with a multivariate logistic regression model to investigate the influencing mechanisms o f passenger flow distribution about land use. Additionally, the study constructs a Space L-weighted subway network that takes into account land, passenger, and locational factors. It proposes network efficiency assessment metrics that balance physical topological features and the impact of land use. Through complex network attack simulations, 14 critical stations with lower weighted network efficiency and higher passenger loss rates are identified. This research offers insights into urban rail transit network land use planning and station layout construction.

articleTitle: Research on task scheduling algorithm of shuttle based storage and retrieval system based on energy consumption
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Shuttle based storage and retrieval system (SBS/RS) has been applied in many automated warehouses because of its high space utilization, flexibility and response speed. The efficiency of task scheduling has a profound impact on the order picking efficiency, customer satisfaction and warehouse operation cost. In this study, based on the indepth analysis of the system operation flow, the service time of all kinds of equipment is calculated, and the equipment energy consumption model is constructed. A task green scheduling model is established to minimize the total energy consumption cost of outbound tasks. An improved particle swarm optimization is used to solve the model and compared with adaptive genetic algorithm and other algorithms to verify model accuracy by several numerical experiments. Low energy consumption can reduce the operating cost and bring more social benefits. The energy consumption costbased task scheduling model proposed in this research provides a new solution to the task scheduling problem.

articleTitle: Research on discrete element parameter calibration of coal based on similarity theory
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: To obtain the optimal combination of discrete element simulation parameters for unscreened bituminous coal, a combination of physical and simulation experiments was used for parameter calibration. A typical particle model with different particle size ranges was established, and the particle size was enlarged by 5 times based on the similarity theory. Three significance variables were determined by Plackett-Burman test, steepest ascent test, and Box-Behnken test. Then the minimum relative error of the experimental and simulation repose angle was taken as the optimization objective to obtain the optimal parameter combination. The physical experiment measured a density of 1.326 t/m3 and static friction coefficients of 0.72 and 0.41 for coal-coal and coal-steel, respectively. The simulation was calibrated to give a Poisson's ratio of 0.4, a shear modulus of 0.67 GPa, rolling friction coefficients of 0.107 and 0.095 for coal-coal and coal-steel respectively, restitution coefficients of 0.5 and 0.15 for coal-coal and coal-steel respectively, and the Johnson Kendall Roberts (JKR) surface energy of 14 J/m2. It is only a 0.58% difference that separates the simulated repose angle of 37.59° from the experimental repose angle of 37.81°, providing the basic parameters for discrete element simulation of bituminous coal with similar characteristics.

articleTitle: Structural parameter optimization design of planetary roller screw pair based on genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Firstly, the basic relationship of structural parameters of planetary roller screw mechanism was analyzed. Secondly, the gear pair parameters were optimized and the genetic optimization algorithm was introduced. The genetic algorithm optimization model was established, including design variables, fitness function, and constraint function, and the genetic optimization algorithm was solved. Finally, based on MATLAB, the gear backlash coefficient of a certain planetary roller screw mechanism was optimized using the genetic optimization method.

articleTitle: Liner wear of large-scale SAG mill Based on DEM analysis
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Liner wear's critical role in semi-autogenous grinding mill design and maintenance is evident, with variable wear across distinct liner structures. Utilizing the discrete element method, we simulated large-scale SAG mill grinding, analyzed composite shell liner wear. Exploring five flat liner configurations’ effects on lifter wear, and three of them were further analyzed. The results showed that wear primarily occurs in grinding and cascading zones, notably higher in upper-left lifters than upper-right, 12.98mm difference. Flat liner structure significantly impacts liner wear rate, particularly during grinding and cascading zone operation. In comparison to YS liner, GJ1 and GJ2 experience 74.2zone and 16.7grinding operation. Furthermore, GJ1 results in a 46.7rate increase in the second wear zone during cascading operation. Considering flat liner structure, transition smoothing near lifter front reduces wear in first wear zone, while similar smoothing near rear increases wear in second wear zone. Convex peaks near lifter front reduce wear in second wear zone.

articleTitle: Dynamic analysis of variable cross-section quayside container crane beams based on improved vector-based finite element method
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: As an important structure for cargo handling in ports and docks, the dynamic performance of quayside cranes is crucial for ensuring efficient loading and unloading operations. This paper presents a dynamic analysis study on the variable cross-section characteristics of quayside crane girders and proposes an improved vector-based finite element method. The method combines optimization algorithms and numerical computation techniques to solve the dynamic response of variable cross-section girders more efficiently. Firstly, a simplified dynamic model of the front girder of the quayside crane is established. Then, based on the improved vector-based finite element method, static and dynamic analyses are conducted on the front girder, and the effectiveness and accuracy of the improved method are validated through comparisons with ANSYS results. The research results demonstrate that the improved vector-based finite element method can accurately simulate the dynamic behavior of quayside crane girders with variable cross-sections. Therefore, this method holds great potential for widespread application in practical engineering scenarios.

articleTitle: Regional gaps and convergence analysis of logistics industry's green welfare effects in China
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: In recent years, logistics industry has been developing quickly in China, and playing a vital role in national economy and society. Meanwhile the logistics industry also brought about carbon emission from the moving trucks, and the wasted corrugated boxes, preventing from establishing green ecosystem associated with better life environment. This paper considers livelihood elements and designs a set of indicators evaluating the green welfare effect of the logistics industry including three dimensions of economic, social and ecological welfare. Using the entropy evaluation method to measure the panel data of China's 30 provinces and cities during 2013-2021, and further adopts the Gini coefficient decomposition method to decompose the regional gaps and explore the reasons for regional gaps. The findings show that: the logistics industry’s welfare level in the eight economic zones as a whole is on an upward trend and shows obvious regional non-equilibrium characteristics; there is a significant spatial heterogeneity of the logistics industry’s green welfare effects among the eight economic zones, and the average annual contribution of interregional disparities reaches 72.3%, which is the main cause of regional disparities. This article aims to provide theoretical guidance for narrowing regional gaps in the logistics industry’s green welfare level and promoting the coordinated regional development of logistics industry.

articleTitle: An intelligent anytime scheduling method for robotic cellular manufacturing systems
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: The work proposes a hybrid search for solving the scheduling problem in robotic cellular manufacturing systems. The proposed approach utilizes a combination of the A∗ approach with a depth-first search to iteratively explore the reachability graph of a place-timed Petri net to obtain transition firing sequences that lead from an original state to a final one. This approach can effectively produce near-optimal solutions within a short computational time, while continuously improving the solution quality as more time is allocated for the search. Experimental evaluations of some example systems have demonstrated the efficacy of the approach.

articleTitle: An empirical analysis of the synergistic development of port logistics and economy in Wuhu city based on the VAR model
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Based on the statistical data of Wuhu City from 2005 to 2021, this paper explores whether there is an interactive relationshi p between the socio-economic development of Wuhu City and port logistics using the analysis results of vector autoregressive model, Granger causality test, impulse response, and variance decomposition. The study shows that there is a two-way causal relationship between Wuhu's economic growth and container cargo throughput, and among the two measures of port logistics, container cargo throughput promotes the city's economy to a more obvious extent and has a longer duration of action. In futur e development, Wuhu City can start from three aspects: promoting the integrated development of the port and city, accelerating the comprehensive strength of port logistics, and establishing a green and long-term development mechanism of port-city synergy to promote better and faster economic development.

articleTitle: Research on location selection of metropolitan area logistics distribution center based on GIS and AHP
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: With the progress and development of technology, the related technologies in the Logistics field have also developed rapidly, and the requirements for the Logistics industry have gradually become higher. The delivery process is one of the key links in Logistics operations, and its location selection is particularly important. This brief study focuses on the Logistics distribution center location problem in the “Wu E Huang Huang” metropolitan area. Based on demand data, distribution center location selection analysis is conducted, and it is taken as the research object. GIS and AHP analysis methods are used to analyze the decision-making of Logistics distribution center location, with a combination of quantitative and qualitative analysis methods has been used to propose some insights and corresponding solutions. These approaches aims to enhance operational efficiency, minimize distribution costs.

articleTitle: Parallel IG algorithm for matrix shop AGV scheduling problem with time and capacity constraints
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: In the current research on scheduling problems, intelligent optimization algorithms have been widely applied by scholars as excellent solutions. The advantage of this method is that it can obtain better solutions for NP-hard problems in a short period of time. The limitation of current optimization methods is that they cannot obtain larger computational space in a short period of time. This paper proposes a parallel iterative greed algorithm (PIGA) that combines intelligent optimization algorithms with parallel computing to achieve larger computational space. In the proposed PIGA, four operators and a restart strategy are used to enhance the algorithm's global and local search capabilities. To verify the performance of the proposed algorithm, PIGA was applied to the matrix workshop automated guided vehicle (AGV) scheduling problem and compared with other optimization algorithms. The experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A rolling horizon optimization for dynamic path planning of multiple warehouse AGVs
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) can improve the efficiency of warehouse picking, but the existing multi-AGV path planning method cannot efficiently solve the collision-free path in the narrow aisle environment. Therefore, a multi-AGV dynamic path planning method with an improved space-time network model is proposed. The proposed method improves the space-time network model, and decomposes the global programming problem with high computational complexity into several local programming models with low complexity, and presents a rolling horizon optimization method for an online solution. The simulation results show that the proposed method is superior to the classical multi-AGV path planning algorithm in terms of total distance and computation time.

articleTitle: Evaluation model of smart port index based on gray entropy variable weight
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: High-performing ports are implementing smart technologies to better manage operations facing stiff competition worldwide. In this context, a framework for smart ports and a quantitative metric, smart port index (SPI), is developed to improve ports resiliency and sustainability. Our proposed SPI is based on key performance indicators (KPIs) based on three key activity domains of a smart port: comprehensive operation, innovation leading and ecological environment. Our methodology provides a gray entropy variable weight method to construct evaluation model for smart ports. Case studies show that the proposed evaluation model can reflect smart level of port comprehensively, systematically, and objectively as well. The results of this study also suggest that government policies and region-specific variables can impact SPI value.

articleTitle: Digital twin workshop architecture design based on UAF
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: The digital twin workshop is an important scene of intelligent manufacturing in the future, which improves the production efficiency of the workshop with its advantage of a combination of virtuality and reality. However, there is still a lack of study on the whole life cycle of digital twin workshop production and the interaction mechanism between the various systems in the workshop. In this view, our paper aims at the architecture of the digital twin workshop. Firstly, we reviewed the works in various business fields of digital twin workshops. Then we introduced the connotation of Unified Architecture Framework (UAF) and proposed the ideas and steps of digital twin workshop architecture design. Finally, the multi-view models of the digital twin workshop architecture were constructed from the perspectives of overview, requirement, operation, strategy, personnel, and resources. This work aims to provide theoretical and application support for developing the digital twin workshop.

articleTitle: Digital track: structural health monitoring for track based on flexible multi-functional sensors
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: With the rapid growth of smart manufacturing and digital technology, it is possible to apply digital twin to structural health monitoring of track. It is difficult to monitor overall perception of the track using traditional sensors and methods with unclear information and low disposal efficiency. Digital twin technology is adopted to real time health data monitoring of track where 3D digital model of track is built on the monitoring terminal. Flexible multi-functional sensors laminated onto the rail waist are used to collect temperature, humidity, stress sensing data of track, which are seen as an interface from actual track to digital track. The visualization sensing data of digital track could be changed simultaneously when the healthy data from the actual track is changed. The sensing position in the 3D digital track is the same to the actual track for precision sensing as the unification of sensor sensing data and spatial scene of digital track. Visualization of digital track with flexible multi-functional sensors could achieve the actual sensing data of track, which has great potential to structural health monitoring of track for the safety evaluation of intelligent transportation system.

articleTitle: Autonomous transport and logistic systems at airports
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic, international air travel came to a stillstand. Therefore, many people lost their job and left the aviation industry. Last year, and in particular this year, with most borders open for international air travel, air traffic volumes grow again and, in some cases, exceed pre-COVID levels. However, due to skilled people having left the aviation industry, there is a serious shortage of staff at airports and airlines. This does not only restrict capacity and leads to unacceptable long queues at airports, but it will also hinder the recovery of the aviation industry. Due to the current staff shortage, airports are looking for technological ways of fulfilling functions previously done by staff and thereby streamlining the transport and logistic processes at airports. One way of doing that, is to use autonomous transport and logistic systems at airports. This paper will discuss current autonomous systems at airports. The discussions will focus on safety and sustainability.

articleTitle: Multi-sensor-based intelligent monitoring system design for hazardous materials warehouse
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Dangerous substances are extremely chemically unstable during storage, and their hazardous properties, such as being flammable, combustible, and corrosive, have stringent storage environment requirements. To strengthen the real-time monitoring of a dangerous goods warehouse, this paper employs IoT technology to design an intelligent monitoring system, selecting ZigBee tree topology to establish a wireless communication link, connect sensor devices, and complete the collection and transmission of monitoring data. In the meantime, the NB-IoT communication module connects to the IoT cloud platform to enable comprehensive remote control and data interaction with monitoring equipment. Through the design of an ethanol monitoring system, experimental cases demonstrate that the system satisfies the requirements for a hazardous materials warehouse monitoring system.

articleTitle: Five-axis multi-direction 3D printing slicing algorithm
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Traditional additive manufacturing (AM) is a layer-by-layer material deposition process, but sometimes it requires the construction of a support structure to complete the corresponding print, and removing the support structure is expensive and time consuming, especially for metal prints. Five-axis additive manufacturing printers have the potential to build structures without the need for support. However, there is a lack of automated process planning software to support the use of five-axis additive manufacturing printers. This paper describes an automated approach: the print needs to be first broken down into sub-volumes so that each sub-volume can be built without support structures in its build direction, and then the corresponding print path is generated by ordering the decomposed volumes while ensuring that there is no local conflict with the previously deposited volumes. The algorithm in this paper realizes a direct print molding.

articleTitle: Research on ceramic 3D printing surface defect detection system based on machine vision
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: A vision-based online surface defect inspection system was developed to identify defects in the ceramic extrusion 3D printing process, consisting mainly of a ceramic 3D printer, a vision inspection platform, and a vision inspection module. By inspecting the surface during the printing process, the inspection system effectively avoids wasted material and time spent doing subsequent processes due to defects arising during the printing process. Image processing is carried out using Halcon software and the area to be detected is extracted using the Otsu method (OSTU) on the acquired images. Defects are detected using methods such as the Canny algorithm and the Fast Fourier Transform, and then the three defects are further differentiated according to feature differences. The experimental results show that the system can detect surface defects with an accuracy of 96.7% or more, which can meet the practical requirements. Using the confusion matrix with recall and accuracy as evaluation metrics for this system, the results show that the inspection system can accurately detect defects that exist in the printing process.

articleTitle: Study on the diffuser structure for broadening flow width and numerical analysis in turbocharger centrifugal compressor
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: The diffuser jets water vapor structure was proposed to deal with the narrow flow range in vehicle turbocharger centrifugal compressor. In this article, the structured grids were meshed by ICEM, a high quality numerical model was established and the improved structure was investigated through multiphase phase numerical simulation with the help of fluent. Comparative analysis was conducted on the performance parameters of compressors under the original and improved structures, as well as the impact of diffuser jets water vapor structure on the flow performance of impeller and volute. The reasons for the improvement of compressor performance due to diffuser jets water vapor structure were analyzed. The result show that, the structure can restrain the expansion of eddy current in the volute, reduce the relative average speed in the impeller outlet, and improve the flow properties of the diffuser. The diffuser jets water vapor structure can increase the flow width and decrease the surge limit traffic, but with the flow range expansion the pressure ratio will decline.

articleTitle: Simulation-based multi-equipment integrated scheduling for a U-shaped container terminal considering uncertain operation times
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: The integrated scheduling problem of container terminals has attracted significant attention in recent years. Uncertainty is frequent in real port terminals, which can increase the scheduling difficulties. It is worthwhile to study the establishment of a more realistic experimental platform that simulates the actual operation scene of the terminal. Visual simulation can play a greater role in this problem than numerical simulation by considering various uncertainties. In this paper, we build a visual simulation platform based on AnyLogic to solve the integrated scheduling problem of quay cranes, intelligent guided vehicles, and yard cranes in a U-shaped container terminal. Uncertain operation times existing in real ports are considered and set in the platform. The simulation platform is used to compare two kinds of robust scheduling plan generation methods: the robust-proactive method considering anti-cascade effects and robustness index proposed by Cai et al and a well-known robust optimization method. Experiments results demonstrate that the RPM-AERI achieves a smaller makespan and provides more effective decision support for port managers.

articleTitle: Analysis of operation modes and equipment configuration in U-shaped sea-rail intermodal port using anylogic simulation
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: There are various types of operation modes for sea-rail intermodal container ports, which significantly influence the overall efficiency of the port. At present, there is no literature available that provides methods on how to select appropriate operation mode for sea-rail intermodal containers, especially on the U-shaped port. Therefore, our study aims to analyze the effects of two different operation modes on the handling efficiency of port: the decentralized operation mode that organizes “train-yard-vessel” and “train-vessel” tasks separately, and the coordinated operation mode that considers all tasks integrally. To quantitatively evaluate the impacts of these operation modes, a simulation model of the U-shaped sea-rail intermodal port is constructed using AnyLogic software. The simulation model employs a coordinated modeling approach that combines multi-agent modeling and discrete event modeling. Moreover, practical implications are provided for port managers regarding the optimal configuration of the number of internal trucks and rail-mounted gantry cranes.

articleTitle: Hierarchical deadlock control of automated manufacturing systems with complex structures
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Deadlock-free operation is a critical objective in automated manufacturing systems (AMSs) to ensure smooth and efficient production processes. While many studies have aimed to obtain computationally tractable and efficient control policies for deadlock resolution, a significant limitation is that they often restrict their models to structurally simple systems. Taking Petri nets (PNs) as a modeling and analysis tool, our focus in this paper is on addressing deadlock resolution for forward-conflict free nets through an on-line distributed control method. One notable advantage of the proposed approach is its ability to enable real-time deadlock avoidance through local observation, control, and execution of processes, without relying on external or extra information about the system. This means that our method can be applied to larger and more intricate manufacturing systems without substantial modifications or loss of efficiency.

articleTitle: Study on the coupling relationship between transport infrastructure and digital economy in the middle and lower reaches of Yangtze river
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: The digital economic system, as a rising financial form, has driven common infrastructure towards technological innovation and cross-border integration through digital technological know-how. As a pioneer in China's economic development, transportation infrastructure improvement plays a crucial role in boosting socioeconomic progress. This article examines the coupled and coordinated relationship between transport infrastructure and the digital economy. Using data from the Yangtze River's central and lower reaches from 2011 to 2019, it explores their interaction from a coupling and coordination perspecti ve. The study finds that the coupling effect between transport infrastructure and the digital economic system in these regions improves annually, forming an efficient coupling effect. Individual analysis reveals higher coupling benefits in the downstream region compared to the midstream region. All provinces and cities develop complementary coupling mechanisms, ultimately achieving high coordination between transport infrastructure and the digital economy.

articleTitle: Literature review of government regulation of online freight platform in China (2016-2022)
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Over the past years, online freight platforms have become increasingly popular in the network industry, driven by the policy of the trial project of Non-Truck Operating Common Carrier(NTOCC) by the ministry of transport of the People's Republic of China. With the rapid development of online freight platforms, problems such as data counterfeiting, fraudulent invoicing and alleged monopoly have emerged one after another. By collecting Chinese and English journal papers from 2016-2022, this paper summarizes and analyzes relevant literatures from two perspectives, i.e., ''research on government regulation at different stages'' and ''research on government regulation with different objectives'', and points out the shortcomings of existing research. Finally, this paper envisioned the research directions and trends of the online freight platform regulation and summarized the interests and demands of the government, society, enterprises and practitioners.

articleTitle: A BERT model-based approach for causation analysis of electric power safety accidents
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: By extracting and classifying the information within accident reports, the process of accident analysis can be made more efficie nt and streamlined. However, the processing of accident reports solely relying on human resources is inefficient and susceptible to subjective judgment, mainly due to the complexity of accident records and varying standards. This paper proposes the BERT model, a deep learning approach based on accident causation theory, to analyze accident reports. Based on the scientific theo ry of accident causation analysis, a dataset of accident causation was created, and the BERT model was fine-tuned to classify the causes and severity levels of accidents. The model was fine-tuned over a range of 1-50 epochs, and it achieved the highest F1 value of 90.24% at the 17th epoch. Furthermore, the Precision and Recall values achieved were 93.29% and 92.71% respectively. Comparison between the BERT model and traditional machine learning models (SVM, Naive Bayes, Random Forest, and Logistic Regression) clearly demonstrates the superior performance of the BERT model. The results of the experiment indicate that the BERT model has better performance than traditional machine learning models in accident causation analysis. This stud y provides a intelligent and efficient method of accident causation analysis for electricity safety regulators.

articleTitle: Research on the friction characteristics of mechanical-hydraulic hybrid vertical lifting system for deep-sea minerals
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Deep-sea mineral resource exploitation is an important field of the mining sector and marine economic strategy. It has far-reaching significance for alleviating the world' s shortage of rare metal resources and guaranteeing sustainable development. However, how to quickly, reliably, and environment-friendly lift wet and sticky deep-sea minerals from seabed to surface production vessels is key technical challenge. In this paper, new type of deep-sea minerals lifting machine-mechanical-hydraulic hybrid vertical lifting system was proposed, and its friction resistance characteristics were studied. A frictional resistance model between minerals and the pipe wall was established based on the Janssen model. The resistance between the minerals and the fluid was established based on the Ergun Equation. The resistance between the fluid and pipeline wall was established based on the Darcy-Weisbach Equation. Finally, a frictional resistance calculation model for the whole system was constructed. A mechanical-hydraulic hybrid lifting experimental device was designed and experiments were conducted to verify the model. The results show that the frictional resistance calculation model matche s to the experimental results reasonably well with an average error of 13.3%. Therefore, the proposed frictional resistance model was verified and can be used to predict the resistance of the mechanical-hydraulic hybrid vertical lifting system.

articleTitle: The application of real-time analysis of 3D point cloud data in safety pre-warning during the construction of mountain tunnels
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Accidents such as collapse, rock burst and water burst happened during the construction of tunnels. The cross-section diagrams of tunnels should be real-time measured to gain the tunnels’ shape changing data and provide the safety pre-warning. Under the help of automatic inspection robot of tunnels, the point cloud data of tunnels’ fracture surface was gained by 3D laser scanner and the cross-section diagrams of tunnels can be created. The traditional point cloud data analysis needs to transport the data from 3D laser scanner to computer, and make offline analysis by special software. This method has the disadvantage in its efficiency, the requirements of the tunnels’ shape changing monitoring can’t be satisfied. The real-time 3D point cloud data analysis technology is designed. The system can automatically collect the point cloud data of tunnel’s fracture surface by 3D laser scanner, through automatic format transformation, data division, point cloud registration and on-line analysis, to output a real-time monitoring data statement and pre-warning message. By field experiment, this technology can increase the timeliness and accuracy of safety pre-warning during the construction of tunnels. This paper can provide the technical support of real-time monitoring of geology deformation during tunnel’s excavation construction.

articleTitle: Aircraft maintenance routing problem model and metaheuristic algorithm
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of civil air transport industry, aircraft maintenance routing problem (AMRP) research has been paid more and more attention. Firstly, this paper proposes an AMRP model that considers both the remaining legal flying time and the remaining legal flying days of aircrafts. Secondly, a hybrid metaheuristic algorithm (GA-CA) based on genetic algorithm and compressed annealing algorithm is proposed to solve the problem. Finally, we carried out two sets of experiments and results showed that the proposed algorithm can obtain high quality solutions in a short time.

articleTitle: Intelligent vibration-monitored data-driven anomaly detection for rolling bearings
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: In the actual industrial environment, the equipment is usually in normal working condition, resulting in the lack of failure modes and data, so it is difficult to establish a mechanical equipment classification and recognition model based on labeled samples. Considering the significant advantages of unsupervised learning in handling unlabeled data, this paper compares four typical detection methods. The article utilizes Fourier Transform to extract 12 frequency domain features from the original vibration signals, representing fault information to assist anomaly detection models. Subsequently, healthy data is used to train the models to obtain anomaly detection thresholds; finally, the detection results are obtained by calculating the scores of the test samples. In the experimental study, the XJTU-SY bearing dataset is selected to compare the detection performance of four typical anomaly detection methods One-Class Support Vector Machine (OCSVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Isolation Forest (iForest). In addition, the early fault location, false alarm number and missing alarm number are used as the index evaluation model. Among them, the iForest anomaly detection method shows excellent anomaly detection performance.

articleTitle: Path planning of mobile robot based on improved D* Lite_TEB algorithm
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: The D*Lite algorithm can address the path planning issue of mobile robot, but generates a path that is not smooth and is close to barriers, which makes collisions likely. To address these issues, a modified algorithm based on D*Lite algorithm and Time Elastic Band (TEB) is presented. The major improvement of the D*Lite algorithm is that remove path redundancy points to shorten the length of path and use B-spline curve to smooth the constrained path. The modified D*Lite algorithm is fused with TEB algorithm to generate a fusion path planning algorithm, which is simulated and verified. The laboratorial results reveal that when the fusion algorithm is applied for path planning, the global path is smooth without collision with obstacles and the local path meets the kinematic constraints of the robot. Compared with a traditional D*Lite algorithm, the path is shortened by 5.3%, the quantity of path nodes is decreased by 96.6% and the quantity of turning times is reduced by 50.0%.

articleTitle: Feature matching research of portal crane based on improved QB-SHOT feature descriptor
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of missing information and low matching rate when using binary azimuth histogram (B-SHOT) for point cloud feature extraction and matching under the complex working conditions of port portal cranes, a B-SHOT feature descriptor (QB-SHOT) based on interval double coding bits is used to carry out feature extraction and feature matching to establish the correspondence between adjacent point clouds. Experimental results show that the improved QB-SHOT algorithm improves the algorithm speed and matching accuracy, and the experimental verification of the feasibility and effectiveness of QB-SHOT application in port portal crane.

articleTitle: The internal flow field analysis of the ultrafine pulverizer based on fluent and the experiment of material classification
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: A series of experiments were carried out on the ultrafine pulverizer, and the ultrafine and uniform material particles were obtained. On the basis of product experiment, the particle size distribution and the optimal cutter speed of 1232 r/min were obtained. In order to study the influence of the speed ratio of cutter head and grading wheel on the crushing and grading effect, Fluent software was used to analyze the flow field state and particle distribution under different working conditions. The results show that in the range of particle size 40µm ~ 900µm, changing the rotation speed of the classifier has a better effect on the classification. When the speed ratio between the cutter head and the grading wheel is 4.11, the maximum particle size of the outlet mass flow is 60µm, which is consistent with the experimental results. Further adjusting the speed ratio to 2.05, 1.37 and 1.23, it is found that the 50µm, 35µm and 30µm particle size of the outlet material account for the highest proportion, and the number of fine particles increases while the particle size decreases. indicating the existence of the optimal cutter head and the grading wheel rotation speed ratio.

articleTitle: Simulation analysis of dynamic scheduling for uncertain task in automated container terminal
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of charging scheduling in automated container terminals, a dynamic charging scheduling strategy is proposed based on the traditional AGV leave when fully charged strategy combined with a new type of horizontal transport vehicle named Unmanned Truck. The strategy is divided into three parts: vehicle rotation, push charging and pull charging. The vehicle rotation strategy divides the vehicles into working vehicles and non-working vehicles for partition management. When the power of the charging vehicle reaches the threshold, the Pull charging strategy will be activated to improve the robustness of the port to deal with unexpected tasks. Finally, the simulation software Anylogic is used to simulate and model the port transportation tasks under different charging scheduling strategies to verify the actual performance of the dynamic charging scheduling strategy.

articleTitle: A review of pallet loading problem with formulations and solutions
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: An optimal or near-optimal solution to Pallet Loading Problems (PLP) can mean high efficiency and low logistics costs in various industry scenarios, such as warehouse management, shipping, and airline cargo transportation. Three-Dimensional Bin Packing Problems (3D-BPP) and Container Loading Problems (CLP) have many commonalities with PLP. Therefore, reviewing their solutions can inspire us to solve PLP. In this paper, we discuss different scenarios of PLP and indicate their various constraints and objectives. Then, we summarize different algorithms and show their advantages and disadvantages. Finally, we discuss the possible future research direction, which can help advance this research field.

articleTitle: Technology foresight research of key technologies for collaborative development of Hainan Port Cluster
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Technology foresight is a tool for strategic management and planning of science, technology and economy.Technology foresight allows for a methodical exploration of long-term development in order to identify key areas of development and emerging technologies that will yield the greatest benefits. In order to promote the collaborative development of Hainan Port Cluster, combined with the current technology application situation, this study designed a technology foresight method combining Delphi method and hierarchical clustering analysis. The key technologies foresight research of the collaborative development of Hainan Port Cluster is carried out. The result identifies the key generic technologies for the collaborative development of Hainan Port Cluster, and analyzes the development level and constraints. According to the survey results, the technologies roadmap of Hainan Port Cluster collaborative development is drawn. It has provided systematic support for the construction of smart ports and the joint construction of ports and cities in Hainan Province.

articleTitle: Mutli-robot path optimization based on DMPC
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Mobile robot path planning refers to the design of the safely collision-free path with shortest distance and least time-consuming from the starting point to the end point by a mobile robot autonomously. At the application of multi-robot pattern formation, when the robot performs path planning in order to reach the target point, there are problems such as many iterations of the algorithm, large errors between the robot and the target point, long paths, and so on. To address these issues, this paper proposes an obstacle avoidance algorithm based on distributed model predictive control (DMPC). This model chooses acceleration as the input of the model, and establishes different constraints and objective functions depending on whether the robot detects other robots or obstacles. Optimal control is performed by optimizing the objective function to obtain the current optimal input. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm in this paper is verified by ex periments, and the results are compared with the Optimal Reciprocal Collision Avoidance (ORCA) algorithm, which shows the advantages of the algorithm in this chapter.

articleTitle: A novel surrogate-assisted differential evolution for mixed-integer expensive constrained optimization problems
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Recently, surrogates have attracted extensive attention due to their ability to combine with evolutionary algorithms to construct high-performance surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithms (SAEAs) for solving expensive constrained optimization problems (ECOPs). Nevertheless, most of these algorithms only focus on the problems with only continuous variables. In order to solve ECOPs with mixed-integer variables, this paper develop a novel surrogate-assisted differential evolution. Firstly, the information of elite solutions and bad solutions is simultaneously utilized in the bad solutions-assisted elite solutions mutation operation to improve the convergence efficiency. Secondly, a multiple mutation operation and a diverse population generation operation are designed to enable the population to jump out of the local optimal region. Therefore, the proposed algorithm has the ability to balance the performance between convergence and global optimization for mixed-integer ECOPs. Finally, experimental studies on ten benchmarks proves the performance of the developed algorithm.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation of lock scheduling considering with ship type standardization for three Gorges-Gezhouba dam cascade hub
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: In order to analyze the effect of standardization of ship types on the actual throughput capacity of Three Gorges-Gezhouba Dam Cascade Hub, a simulation model based on multi-agent method is established to simulate the whole process of shipping lockage by the Anylogic simulation tool. The main navigation facilities are built in the simulation model to reflect the actual process. Based on operational history data, the experiment with different rates of standardization ship in ship traffic flow are designed. The throughput capacity and chamber utilization area of the cascade reservoirs are calculated in different cases. From the experiment results, it can be seen that the standardization rate of ship type reaches 90% or more, the advantage of standard ship type to improve the operation efficiency of locks is obvious.

articleTitle: Fabrication of microscale silver conductive structures by electric field-driven direct writing
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: The electrohydrodynamic (EHD) printing technology has great potential in micro/nano manufacturing. However, due to the electrostatic repulsion between conductive particles, the EHD cannot form a jet stably using conductive materials. Herein, an improved electric field-driven direct writing (EDW) method is proposed, which utilizes the Taylor cone in contact with substrates to print directly but not form a jet. This strategy avoids the unstable electric jet printing with conductive ink and enables the fabrication of micro-scale, large-area conductive structures. In this study, the effects of printing speed on the line width, resistance of the Ag nanoparticles (AgNPs) and Ag nanowires (AgNWs) conductive structures were investigated. The mechanism of AgNWs arrangement and the relationship between arrangement and resistivity was also deeply analyzed. The final fabricated AgNPs and AgNWs conductive structures were with minimum line widths of 81.0 μm and 78.6 μm, the resistivities of 8.40 × 10-7 Ω·m and 7.78 × 10-7 Ω·m separately. Furthermore, interdigital electrodes with a line width of 380 μm were fabricated using AgNPs ink, and flexible electrodes which can maintain stable resistance when bent at 180° were printed with AgNWs ink. This demonstrated the good applicability of EDW printing in the fabrication of microscale silver conductive structures.

articleTitle: Human-centric interoperability method for greenhouse digital twins in metaverse era
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: With the emerging of Digital twins (DT) and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies in the field of smart agriculture, the agricultural metaverse (AM) is becoming a research hotspot currently. Massive networked and smart sensors and agricultural robots are deployed in greenhouses, and factory greenhouses have become one of the most promising AM application scenarios. Therefore, this paper explores a human-centric interoperability method for the greenhouse DT, in the era of the future AM. First, a smart greenhouse DT model is built, including greenhouse DTs, crop growth models, and facility control modules; Second, based on the greenhouse DT, a human-centered interoperability framework is proposed for socialized greenhouses. Finally, a prototype system of greenhouse DT is designed, to verify the feasibility of the human-centered interoperability method.

articleTitle: A reachability-decidable petri net modeling method and its application to flexible manufacturing systems
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: Petri nets (PNs) are graphical and mathematical tools used to model various discrete event systems and analyze their properties. Reachability is their fundamental property. When we use a state equation to determine a state’s (marking’s) reachability, the existence of legal firing sequences (LFSs) corresponding to nonnegative integer solutions (NISs) of the state equation needs to be determined. Our previous work has proposed an algorithm to determine the LFSs’ existence in polynomial time. However, when a state equation has an infinite number of NISs, we cannot check all NISs to determine a marking’s reachability. Hence, this work studies the relationship between the structure of an ordinary PN and the number of NISs of its state equation. Then, a method is proposed to modify the structure of the PN such that the state equation has no more than one NIS. The modified PN is used as the final model of the system, which maintains the functions of its modeled system. Its reachability can be determined in polynomial time. This work shows the application of the proposed method to a flexible manufacturing system’s modeling and analysis.

articleTitle: Distribution of cruise ports in the Mediterranean region: spatial heterogeneity and influencing factors
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: To reveal the geographical rules of the development of cruise ports in the Mediterranean region, this study systematically analyzed the functional types and spatial characteristics of cruise ports in the Mediterranean region. The results show that: (1) the distribution of 253 cruise ports shows a pattern of more in the east and less in the west, more in the north and less in the south, and forming a high-density cluster of four ports on the north coast. (2) The ratio of port of the departure port and the port of call is 1:5. The main types of departure ports are mainland coastal types, while the number of island types and mainland coastal types is relatively uniform in the port of call. The selection of departure ports by cruise operators is characterized by high overlap and partial specificity. (3) At the intercontinental and national scales, the spatial distribution range of the port of call is wider and denser than that of the departure port. (4) The differences in port facilities and traffic conditions, economic development between countries and regions, geopolitical and national stability, and port and navigation relations profoundly affect the spatial differentiation pattern of cruise ports in the Mediterranean region.

articleTitle: Human-robot collaborative picking optimization in robotic mobile fulfillment systems
publicationTitle: International Conference on Automation in Manufacturing, Transportation and Logistics (iCaMaL 2023)
abstract: In a robotic mobile fulfillment system, mobile robots transport pods containing commodities from storage areas to a picking station, where a human picker works to fulfill orders. Such a human-robot cooperative operation process leads to optimization problems of pod selection, multi-robot task allocation, and picking scheduling. This work focuses on their joint optimization to minimize makespan, i.e., the completion time of the last order-picking task. To efficiently solve the concerned problem, this work adapts a Tabu search algorithm by introducing problem-specific encoding and decoding procedures, variable tabu duration, and memory-based penalty moves. Experimental results indicate the significant advantages of the designed algorithm in solving accuracy and stability compared with other intelligent optimization algorithms.
